content.thinking:
I'm sorting the decision order as reject, escalate, return, incomplete, then approve, with the order taken from SOP 2.1. For the unknowns case I'm pulling in SOP 2.2, which says a claim with an unknown required fact can't be approved and should be marked incomplete. I'm now checking the first rule in Section 3, where a submission at 61 or more days gets rejected.

I'm checking the rule for self-approved claims and the escalation rule for claims of $5,000 or more without the Finance Director's sign-off. I'm also going through the receipt, alcohol, and gift rules in Section 4.

I'm checking the business-class airfare exception in 4.5, which allows pre-approved business-class airfare to be approved. It conflicts with the 4.4 escalation rule, and since escalate ranks above approve in the order, I'm working out how that exception plays out.

I'm weighing whether the 4.5 approve rule would ever change an outcome, since any claim it covers also hits the 4.4 escalation for business-class airfare, and escalate ranks above approve. So it can't alter the result, and I'm leaning toward keeping it as written and noting the conflict.

I'm now deciding how to handle the lines collection: the SOP only says a claim is a list of lines, one per receipt or expense, and gives no rule for when it counts as empty, so I'm treating an empty claim as unknown and citing SOP 1 for that. I'm also confirming the pre-approval fact matches the wording about pre-approval in writing from the Finance Director.

I'm listing the sections I still need to cover in the sources: section 1, the two Section 2 subsections, the Section 3 rules, and the five Section 4 rules. The claim totals are already given, so no sums are needed and the computed list stays empty. I'm also wondering whether any case-word mappings are needed, but I don't think so.

I'm adding a small cabin mapping so "business class" and "first-class" both resolve to the SOP's business and first values, and I'm checking that the receipt and amount rules still line up with the claim facts.

I'm checking the wording of the 3.1 text against the SOP, comparing the exact sentences about the 60-day limit and the 61-day rejection.

I'm writing the business-class airfare approve rule for 4.5 and noting that it is always overridden by the 4.4 escalation, since escalate ranks above approve.

unknowns.text: If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the claim cannot be approved.

lines.unknown_when_empty: which lines (receipts or expenses) the claim has
lines.text: A claim is a list of lines, one per receipt or expense.

rules.text: Claims must be submitted within 60 days of the earliest expense on them. Reject a claim submitted 61 days or more after its earliest expense.
A claim's approver must not be the employee who submitted it. Reject a self-approved claim.
A claim totalling $5,000 or more needs the Finance Director's sign-off. Without it, escalate.
Every line of $75 or more needs an itemised receipt. If a receipt is missing or has not been attached, return the claim.
Alcohol is not reimbursable. Return any claim with a line for alcohol.
A gift to a government official must be reviewed under the anti-bribery policy. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class and first-class airfare must be reviewed. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class airfare pre-approved in writing by the Finance Director may be approved.

sections.note: Defines the five outcomes. Incomplete is used as the unknowns outcome. The sentence that defines a claim as a list of lines is the source of the lines collection.
Sets the treatment of unknown facts (unknowns -> incomplete).

This is translated as written. Any line it matches also matches 4.4 (premium-cabin-airfare). Under 2.1, escalate is more severe than approve, so this rule can never decide a claim. The SOP contradicts itself here, and a person must decide whether 4.5 should be an exception to 4.4.
